## Introduction

This report checks the particle filter's likelihood estimate by running it many
times at the He et al. (2010) maximum likelihood estimates for two towns: London,
the largest unit, and Halesworth, one of the smallest. Only the random seed
varies across replicates, so any systematic difference between `pypomp` and
`pomp` would be a difference between the implementations.

We run `pypomp` twice, once in single precision and once in double precision. We
have seen some indication that single precision slightly shifts the estimated
log-likelihood for the measles model, so we check that here. Since `pomp` uses
double precision throughout, the 64-bit run is the direct comparison with
`pomp`, while the 32-bit run shows the effect of `pypomp`'s default precision.

```{python Load results}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import checks
from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_density, facet_wrap, labs

os.environ["JAX_PLATFORMS"] = "cpu"

PLATFORMS = {
    "R pomp": os.path.join("results", "R"),
    "pypomp (32-bit)": os.path.join("results", "f32"),
    "pypomp (64-bit)": os.path.join("results", "f64"),
}
runs = ru.load_timing_data(PLATFORMS)

frames = []
for label, d in PLATFORMS.items():
    df = ru.read_if_exists(os.path.join(d, "pfilter_logliks.csv"))
    if df is not None:
        df = df[["unit", "replicate", "logLik"]].copy()
        df["source"] = label
        frames.append(df)

combined = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True) if frames else pd.DataFrame(
    columns=["unit", "replicate", "logLik", "source"]
)
units = sorted(combined["unit"].unique())


def ll(unit, source):
    return combined[(combined["unit"] == unit) & (combined["source"] == source)]["logLik"].values
```

## Automated checks

Only the 64-bit comparisons receive a verdict. The 32-bit rows report the shift
due to single precision for reference.

```{python Automated checks, results='asis'}
M_TESTS = 2 * len(units)
level = checks.run_level(runs)
rows = []
for arm, verdict in [("pypomp (64-bit)", True), ("pypomp (32-bit)", False)]:
    for unit in units:
        rows += checks.loglik_checks(
            ll(unit, arm), ll(unit, "R pomp"), f"{unit}: {arm} vs R pomp", M_TESTS, verdict=verdict
        )
rows = checks.gate_smoke(rows, level)
checks.save(rows, level, pypomp_version=runs["pypomp (64-bit)"]["meta"].get("pypomp_version"))
display(HTML(checks.table_html(rows, M_TESTS)))
```

## Visual review

- [Density comparison](#density-comparison): within each town, the 64-bit and `pomp` densities should overlap heavily. Since the 32-bit and 64-bit runs differ only in precision, any shift of the 32-bit density away from the other two should be due to precision rather than the filter.

---

## Summary statistics

We include `logmeanexp`, the log of the mean likelihood, since it is the
likelihood estimate that `pomp` reports.

```{python Summary table}
summary = (
    combined.groupby(["unit", "source"])["logLik"]
    .agg(
        n="count",
        mean="mean",
        sd="std",
        min="min",
        max="max",
        logmeanexp=ru.logmeanexp,
    )
    .reset_index()
    .sort_values(["unit", "source"])
)

display(HTML(summary.round(3).to_html(classes="table table-striped table-hover", index=False)))
```

## Density comparison

```{python Density plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6}
(
    ggplot(combined, aes(x="logLik", fill="source", color="source"))
    + geom_density(alpha=0.35)
    + facet_wrap("~unit", scales="free")
    + labs(
        title="Particle filter log-likelihood at the He et al. (2010) estimates",
        subtitle="One density per implementation, per town",
        x="Log-likelihood",
        y="Density",
        fill="Source",
        color="Source",
    )
    + ru.scale_fill_premium()
    + ru.scale_color_premium()
    + ru.theme_premium
)
```
